summary: Nvidia rehires its ousted CEO, NATO sends a radar plane to Poland, Iran claims mine strikes under US pressure, Gaza's disarmament plan stalls, Korea's exam minister quits, and an AI-made proof awaits checks.

question.text: Today asks you to trust checks you cannot see: officials saying a CEO poses "no security risk", Iran saying mines hit three tankers, and a computer saying 17 million lines of proof are correct. For each, who did the checking, and what would make you believe it?

read.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
read.summary: A clear look at how an AI system proved a major result in number theory, what mathematicians think of it, and why they still want proofs humans can understand.

topics.heading: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as CEO, and its shares jump about 30%
topics.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang on Monday, 11 days after he resigned, saying senior US officials told it his return poses "no national security risk".[^1][^2] Shares closed up about 31%, and government and board investigations continue.[^3][^1]

lead.title: Nvidia stocks soar after Jensen Huang reinstated as chief executive
lead.outlet: ABC News (Australia), with Reuters and AFP

alsoReported.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following US national security review

article: Nvidia makes most of the chips that train and run today's AI, which has made it one of the world's most valuable companies. On Nov 12 its co-founder and chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a businesswoman whom US authorities suspected of spying for China. Beijing denies the spying claims.[^1]

On Monday the board reversed course and voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president and director. It said it had received input from "senior levels" of the US government and was confident his return poses no national security risk.[^2] A week earlier the board had said it did not plan to bring him back.[^1] President Trump praised the decision and said the attorney general had confirmed there was no evidence of unlawful conduct; that is his account, not a published finding.[^1]

Investors cheered. Fox News reports the stock closed up about 31%, adding roughly $950 billion in market value in a day, after a broad sell-off in AI stocks last week.[^3] The board also set up a committee on national security and export controls, is hiring a new chief compliance officer, and says its own inquiry into whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort will continue.[^2] ABC reports that investigations by the SEC and the Justice Department are still under way.[^1]

Critics in both parties question the speed of the reversal. Senator Elizabeth Warren called it "reckless", and Republican Senator John Cornyn asked, "No national security risk? Based on what?"[^1] Huang is due before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec 3.[^3]
My read: markets have answered the leadership question for now, but the harder questions about chip exports to China are moving to Congress, where Democrats take control in January.
topics.differences: The board and the White House say the government found no security risk; critics, including Republicans Don Bacon and John Cornyn, say no evidence for that has been made public.[^1][^2]

topics.heading: NATO sends an early-warning plane to Poland after Russian missiles land there
topics.summary: After an emergency meeting on Monday, NATO approved sending an AWACS early-warning aircraft to Poland and is weighing more assets, following the Nov 20 crash of Russian cruise missiles on Polish soil.[^4][^6] Poland now says all three objects were Russian Kh-101 missiles.[^4]

lead.title: NATO to send surveillance aircraft to Poland after Russian missile strikes

alsoReported.title: NATO to Offer Poland 'Strong Support' After Russian Missiles Enter Its Airspace
NATO Eyes New European Force Moves Following Russian Breach of Polish Skies

article: Yesterday's brief covered the start of this meeting. Background: on Nov 20, during a large Russian attack on western Ukraine, three objects crossed into southeastern Poland and came down at three sites. No one was hurt.[^5] On Sunday Poland said all three were Kh-101 cruise missiles, and early findings suggest they were made recently in Russia.[^4]

NATO ambassadors met in Brussels on Monday at Poland's request. NATO's spokeswoman said its top commander in Europe had authorised the forward deployment of an AWACS plane, a radar aircraft that can spot low-flying missiles far beyond the range of ground radar, and was "examining the deployment of additional assets".[^4][^6] NATO said Russia "bears full responsibility".[^4] Poland's deputy defence minister called it "a very serious capability" and stressed it was not an offensive step.[^4]

Why the missiles were not stopped matters for the next steps. Swedish fighter jets flying for NATO were cleared to fire, but bad weather meant pilots could not confirm what they were chasing in time.[^4][^5] On Monday night a Russian drone entered Polish airspace from Ukraine for several minutes; Poland held fire when it turned back, citing the risk to civilians.[^4] Russia has not commented on either incident.[^4]

My read: this is a measured response. NATO is improving its ability to see threats rather than escalating, but repeated incursions keep raising the question of how allies would react if one caused casualties.
topics.differences: Poland's prime minister has suggested the incursion may have been a deliberate provocation, and a deputy minister said an accident is "difficult to imagine"; no public evidence has settled whether it was deliberate.[^4][^5]

topics.heading: Iran says three tankers hit mines in Hormuz as US sanctions squeeze its economy
topics.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers caught fire after hitting mines while sailing under US protection; the claim is unverified.[^8][^7] Washington added sanctions on Iran's informal banking network, and Iranian leaders talk of breaking the blockade by force.[^9][^7]

lead.title: Is Iran weighing tanker convoy to break US blockade?

alsoReported.title: IRGC: Three oil tankers hit mines, caught fire while transiting Hormuz with US support - report
Middle East conflict: US investigates Iran over cyberattacks on 50 ships as fresh sanctions target Iran's shadow banking network

article: Since the spring, the US Navy has blockaded Iran's ports, halting its oil exports, while Iran controls traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow route for about a fifth of the world's oil. On Tuesday Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said three "violating" tankers had exploded and caught fire after hitting mines, and that US escorts had not protected them.[^8] US Central Command had not responded, and the claim has not been independently confirmed.[^8][^7]

Attacks on ships are already at a wartime high: the UK's maritime agency counted more than 30 in October and at least 22 in November by Sunday.[^8] The Wall Street Journal reports the US is also investigating whether Iran hacked up to 50 commercial ships.[^9]

On Monday the US Treasury sanctioned 22 companies and 8 people it says form Iran's "shadow banking" system, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Iran's leaders are "panicking".[^9][^7] Iran's own figures show heavy strain: inflation hit 88.7% in October and there are power cuts.[^7] Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said there are "military ways to break the blockade"; state TV denied that a tanker convoy had set sail.[^7]

Iran says Hormuz could reopen within two days if the US lifts the blockade and meets its other demands.[^10] Qatar is trying to revive talks; its prime minister met Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Monday and urged against escalation.[^9]
My read: both sides are betting the other will crack first. The danger is a clash at sea, for example over an Iranian tanker convoy, that neither side planned.
topics.differences: The IRGC says mines hit three tankers; The National notes that maritime reports on other recent incidents described unidentified projectiles, not confirmed mines.[^7][^8] The US says sanctions are working, while Iran calls the blockade "military aggression".[^9][^10]

topics.heading: Board of Peace says Hamas agreed to a disarmament roadmap, but little has moved
topics.summary: The US-led Board of Peace says Hamas and other factions agreed in July to a 15-point plan to give up weapons, but that progress on the ground is limited.[^11] Israeli strikes killed at least three people in Gaza on Monday, including a UN aid worker.[^12]

lead.title: Hamas, Palestinian factions agree to Gaza disarmament roadmap, Board of Peace says

alsoReported.title: Israeli strikes kill at least 3 in Gaza, including worker with UN Palestinian agency
Jared Kushner sees two paths for Israel: Security or 'global pariah status'

article: The Board of Peace was set up under a UN Security Council resolution to oversee Gaza after the October 2025 ceasefire. On Monday it said Hamas and other Palestinian factions had agreed on July 30 to a 15-point roadmap to hand over weapons and pass power to a transitional Palestinian administration, but that implementation remains limited.[^11] That committee has hired staff and drafted a six-month rebuilding plan, but works little on the ground.[^11]

Its report to the Security Council warned that a ceasefire "that delivers nothing visible" cannot last forever, and said Israel's delays in approving the new governing bodies and a civilian police force are, in effect, leaving Hamas in charge.[^14] Israel argues the plan would not lead to full disarmament and wants that first, before any withdrawal.[^14][^13]

Daily life remains hard. Storms on Nov 6 to 8 flooded thousands of tents.[^11] Israel's aid agency, COGAT, says nearly 100,000 tents have entered Gaza and that 67,000 more approved tents have not been brought in, which it blames on Hamas.[^11] On Monday strikes killed at least three people, including a worker for UNRWA, the UN agency for Palestinians. Since the ceasefire, at least 1,600 Palestinians and five Israeli soldiers have been killed, by each side's count, and Israeli troops now hold about two-thirds of Gaza.[^12]

US envoy Jared Kushner told New York Magazine that Israel faces a "fork in the road" between security and "global pariah status".[^13] My read: little will move until Israel forms a new government after its inconclusive October election.
topics.differences: The Board of Peace blames slow progress mainly on Israeli delays and Hamas's unfinished disarmament; Israel says Hamas must disarm fully first; COGAT says Hamas is blocking shelter deliveries.[^11][^14]

topics.heading: South Korea's education minister quits over chaotic anti-AI-cheating rules for a key exam
topics.summary: Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday after last-minute rules to stop AI-assisted cheating on the national university entrance exam caused confusion.[^15][^16] President Lee Jae Myung accepted within an hour and says AI cheating is spreading to other tests.[^15][^16]

lead.title: Education minister resigns amid backlash over CSAT anti-cheating measures

alsoReported.title: Lee accepts education minister's resignation after CSAT anticheating measures trigger nationwide confusion

article: South Korea's CSAT, held on Nov 19, decides university places for a whole year group, so it is treated almost as a national event. This year officials feared AI cheating after the top scorer on a tax accountants' exam admitted on Nov 15 to using a tiny camera and AI.[^15]

Two days before the CSAT, the ministry added 8,400 staff, including about 1,800 to detect smart devices. Students were told to cover clothing buttons with stickers, and the day before, items that had been allowed, such as correction tape, erasers and some pens, were banned.[^15] The ministry later said it had caught 111 suspected cases of cheating with electronic devices.[^16]

Minister Choi had told lawmakers he did not think he could stop AI cheating, "perhaps because of my age", which drew wide criticism.[^15] He then mostly stayed out of sight until the exam.[^17] On Sunday he said he felt responsible for failing to prepare.[^16] The opposition says resigning is not enough and wants an investigation.[^15]

President Lee said AI cheating is spreading to essay admissions and school tests, and ordered a review of marking exam papers to identify them.[^16] My read: schools everywhere face the same problem. Wearable cameras and AI make old exam rules hard to enforce, and rushed fixes can hurt honest students most.

topics.heading: A mathematician says he and an AI proved the Riemann hypothesis; experts are checking
topics.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, posted a claimed proof of the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis made with the AI Claude and backed by a huge computer-checked proof.[^18] Leading mathematicians say it is far from accepted.[^18]

lead.title: Riemann hypothesis has puzzled scientists for 167 years. Has AI solved it?

article: The Riemann hypothesis, posed in 1859, is a statement about where a special function's zeros lie, and it is closely tied to how prime numbers are spread out. It is one of the Clay Institute's million-dollar "Millennium Problems" and is often called the most famous open problem in mathematics.[^18]

On Nov 20 Alpöge published a four-page document saying that, with Claude, he believes he has a proof. He reportedly also submitted about 17 million lines of code in Lean, a program that checks each step of a proof mechanically, and an MIT mathematician confirmed the code runs.[^18] Disclosure: this brief is also written with Claude's help, so weigh my framing with that in mind.

Running the code is not the same as a proof everyone accepts. Experts must check that the code proves exactly the right statement, without hidden assumptions or changed definitions, and a proof is usually expected to be explained so humans can follow it. Fields medallist James Maynard said a confirmed proof would be historic; Andrew Granville criticised how unclear the document is, and Alpöge has promised a clearer write-up.[^18] Separately, a human-written draft proof of a broader version, shared by the head of the American Mathematical Society, already has possible problems flagged.[^18]

Context: in October an OpenAI system proved a weaker "quasi" version, which mathematicians called a major result but which senior experts would not treat as settled until people understood every step.[^19] My read: whether or not this claim holds, AI is changing how mathematics is done, and the question of how humans trust proofs they cannot read is now real.
topics.differences: Only one outlet I could open confirms the details of the Nov 20 claim; others were blocked. Supporters point to the machine check; critics say a proof that no human can follow is not yet accepted knowledge.[^18]
